newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C. BANK TO LAUNCH REPO AUCTION ON JUNE 4.
newsitem.headline: C. BANK TO LAUNCH REPO AUCTION ON JUNE 4.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Monday that it will organise its first repo auction on June 4 with the lowest interest rate set at seven percent, the maximum amount of 20 million litas and maturity of seven working days.

"The Bank of Lithuania, in an attempt to evaluate the readiness and the need of commercial banks for open market operations, will organise its first repo auction on June 4," the bank said in a statement.
The bank said that the securities will be repurchased in seven working days and the lowest interest rate for the deal will be seven percent.
The bank also said that the maximum sum commercial banks will be offered will not exceed 20 million litas.
The time table for further auctions will established in the future, the bank said.
"Such auctions are an integral part of the first stage of the central bank's monetary policy for 1997-1999," the bank added.

The central bank plans to gradually scrap the currency board system, which rigidly pegs the litas to the U.S. dollar at a rate of four to one, and regain control of classic monetary policy instruments.
